items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master of Public Health (MPH), Master’s degree in Higher Education Administration, Student Affairs, or a closely related field.
2 - 4 years of related experience.
Minimum of 2 years of recent experience as a professional level student affairs officer or equivalent in a research university setting, effectively advising and counseling students.
Prior experience with Banner student information system.
Recent University of California experience as a professional level student affairs officer or equivalent.
Demonstrated experience with UC policies and procedures.

Academic Advising & Progress Tracking: Provides routine academic, programmatic, and foundational career advising to new and continuing graduate students within the department. Assists students with degree progress tracking, major/concentration requirements, course scheduling, and navigating University or Grad Division policies. Monitors student programs and prepares required milestone documentation for MPH including Capstone/Thesis Projects, Comprehensive Fieldwork Reports, etc. Ensures that final culminating projects or exam records are complete and accessible to the faculty review team. Reviews student records to identify academic progression or GPA issues and coordinates standard interventions under the guidance of the Graduate Advisor. Advises students on standard professional norms, resume preparation, and interviewing processes specific to public health career pathways. (25% time)

Admissions Processing: Coordinates the graduate admissions pipeline and supports the department's holistic review process for applicants. Corresponds with applicants to interpret admission policies, clarify regulations, and provide status updates on application completeness. Advises prospective applicants on necessary academic preparation and the alignment of the MPH program with their professional goals. Reviews and evaluates domestic transcripts for degree eligibility. Coordinates a holistic screening of applications by assessing qualitative and quantitative records—including GPAs, letters of recommendation, professional/community experience, and personal statements—to identify alignment with faculty specialties and department areas of emphasis. Utilizes established departmental systems to ensure consistent and reliable circulation of applicant files to the faculty admissions committee. (20% time)

Program Administration & Database Maintenance: Applies professional student services concepts to provide a full range of administrative support to the student population, faculty, and management within the organization. Serves as a recognized resource of program knowledge, reviewing and implementing procedures for handling program processes and exceptions under the guidance of the Graduate Program Director. Serves as a primary liaison with other departments to resolve day-to-day administrative and operational issues. Coordinates quarterly teaching assistant meetings, schedules and attends Graduate Advisory/Admissions Committee meetings, and participates in various MPH-related committee meetings. Independently maintains, updates, and updates departmental databases and spreadsheets; prepares reports and provides statistical, placement, and procedural data to program Chairs and SOM leadership as needed. Performs enrollment management duties, reviews the campus General Catalog, and certifies classes through the Course and Instruction Reporting System. (15% time)

Financial Aid & Appointment Processing: Coordinates the graduate student financial support pipeline, reviewing fellowship allocations, grants, and funding packages for compliance with campus, state, and federal guidelines. Participates in the processing, evaluation, and awarding of departmental fellowships and awards, and advises students on standard financial aid options. Initiates program financial support tracking and monitors spending to ensure the optimal, timely, and compliant use of funds in alignment with the operating budget and project goals. Coordinates with leadership to ensure that modifications to student financial packages are sustainable given department and program resources. Manages administrative processes, tracking, and paperwork required for academic student employee appointments, including Graduate Student Researchers (GSRs), Teaching Assistants (TAs), Readers, and Tutors. (15% time)

Student Recruitment and Event Operations: Coordinates student recruitment, outreach, and event operations for the MPH program. Designs, develops, and distributes targeted recruitment materials, including newsletters, program announcements, event calendars, posters, and digital content. Represents the department and the School of Medicine (SOM) at outreach events and college fairs to communicate information regarding admissions criteria, curricular options, housing, and fellowships. Coordinates comprehensive campus visit logistics for prospective graduate students. Plans, implements, and manages logistics for standard student events—such as orientations, open houses, and info sessions—and assists leadership with the execution of highly complex events such as commencement/hooding. Collaborates with SOM partners to organize and coordinate graduate student social, cultural, and leadership development programs. (10% time)

Practicum Coordination: Coordinates operational logistics for student placements at external practicum and fieldwork sites. Serves as the primary administrative point of contact for external site partners and preceptors to coordinate placement schedules. Gathers necessary organizational metrics, contact information, and scope-of-work details required to initiate institutional affiliation agreements, routing complete profiles to leadership for contract execution. Monitors ongoing student placement logs and maintains up-to-date site data and partner contact records in departmental databases. Administers and tracks mandatory pre- and post-placement evaluation metrics, including distributing and compiling post-practicum preceptor surveys to ensure continuous program compliance and quality control. (10% time)

Student Life, Conduct, & Compliance Liasison: Serves as the primary departmental resource and liaison on matters regarding student conduct, academic integrity, and university policies. Provides guidance to students and faculty regarding organization policies and procedures on student conduct, and routes complex grievances or disciplinary issues to central campus compliance offices. Independently develops, edits, and maintains the program's official academic literature, assuring that the MPH student handbook accurately reflects current degree requirements, university regulations, and designated emphasis guidelines. Manages the administrative tracking and compliance pipeline for student onboarding requirements, ensuring all incoming students complete mandatory university trainings, health clearances, and background checks required for departmental enrollment. (5% time)

Ability to interpret and apply federal, state and UC regulations pertaining to student records and confidentiality, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA). Ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
Knowledge of complex U.S. visa and immigration procedures, compliance issues, and employment eligibility/authorization for international students and scholars.

Excellent writing skills to produce spreadsheets, reports, instructional brochures, booklets, handout materials, and various forms of communication including promotional information, website content, announcements, correspondence, etc.
Strong computer proficiency in MS Office applications, online business systems and online student information systems. Demonstrated experience working in a student information/records system.
Ability to multi-task; verbal and written communication skills.
Strong interpersonal skills.
Demonstrated organization and prioritization skills necessary to meet daily, weekly and monthly deadlines.
Working knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.
Ability in problem identification and reasoning; ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Multicultural competencies; ability to work with diverse populations.
Skills in judgment and decision-making, problem solving, identifying measures of system performance and the actions to improve performance.

Knowledge of University-specific computer application programs and knowledge of University and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
